title: Tesla Takedown - Stanford Mall
description:
CALSTRS and CALPERS: Divest from Tesla Funds NOW!

STOP THE BILLIONAIRE TAKEOVER. WE ARE THE MANY. THEY ARE THE FEW. JOIN US.

This is a peaceful demonstration, and any conflicts or altercations will not be tolerated. Walk away if one arises and report it to the demonstration leader on site if it is a serious altercation. We will comply with requests from the police, including if we are asked to leave.

Do not boo or confront Tesla drivers or cars, or Tesla employees. Remember that most Tesla drivers are our allies, and many are protesting with us!

No one voted for Musk. Join the peaceful Tesla Takedown movement!

In solidarity, please add #LatinoFreeze or #LatinoFreezeMovement to placards.

Free Ulises, Free Kilmar, Free Khalil. Free them all! 

Elon Musk is destroying our democracy, and he's using the fortune he built at Tesla to do it. We are taking nonviolent action at Tesla to stop Musk's illegal coup.

⚡Sell your Teslas, dump your stock, join the picket lines.

⚡ We're tanking Tesla's stock price to stop Musk.

⚡Stopping Musk will help save lives and protect our democracy.

The stakes couldn’t be higher. No one is coming to save us. Not politicians, not the media, not the courts.

Tesla Takedown is a peaceful protest movement. We oppose violence, vandalism and destruction of property. This protest is a lawful exercise of our First Amendment right to peaceful assembly.

Wear Orange for National Gun Violence Awareness Week and/or colors of the rainbow for Pride month

https://wearorange.org/

#TeslaTakedown #BoycottTesla #DueProcess #LatinoFreeze

title: Indivisible TX-24 Elon's Birthday #MuskorUs Protest __ Southlake
description:
Worldwide Day of Birthday Actions for Elon!!! we will then be continuing on each Saturday for our weekly protest! Elon is not gone, just a more maniacal billionaire out of control. Keep showing up as his actions are illegal, hurt us and enrich him and his billionaire friends.

Take Peaceful Protest Action at Tesla showrooms everywhere, including Southlake.

Making Musk toxic will help save jobs, lives and our democracy.

The stakes couldn’t be higher. No one is coming to save us—not politicians, not the media. So take pictures use #NoKings #MuskOrUs 
Your courage is contagious. Showing up builds community and constituent power. 

Important Guidelines
Public Space Only: Stay on sidewalks and public areas—do not block business entrances or trespass on private property. Please follow all state and local regulations regarding gathering on public and private property.
Stay on Message: This is about Musk’s political takeover, not Tesla, SpaceX, or X as companies.
Indivisible is focused on Musk’s role in the Trump-Musk billionaire coup. 
Indivisible is not advising and does not condone any actions that directly interfere with the daily operations or activities of any business or entity. Please follow all state and local guidelines regarding gathering on public or private business property. 
A core principle behind all Musk or Us events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values, and to act lawfully at these events. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

Join Indivisible TX-24 and allies. Be Peaceful. Take pics and video
#muskorus #nokings

title: Croton, NY: Pass a Resolution Against Project Maple
description:
**Join us outside the Croton Board of Trustees meeting to demand local action against Project Maple** — a dangerous fracked gas pipeline expansion plan that threatens our climate, our river, and our health.

Fossil Fuel company Enbridge's Project Maple would expand the amount of fracked gas running through the existing Algonquin Pipeline (which runs through Westchester County) by replacing existing pipe and expanding compressor stations. 

This project would lock us into decades of fossil fuel dependence — just when we need to be transitioning to clean energy. It’s risky, unnecessary, and completely out of step with New York’s climate goals. **Croton has the chance to be a climate leader by passing a resolution opposing this reckless project.**

Meet us outside Croton-on-Hudson Village Hall, where we’ll rally together, then head into the board meeting to make powerful public comments demanding the Village take a stand.

Let’s pack the room and show our elected officials that Croton stands for climate justice, not fossil fuel expansion. Bring your friends, your voice, and your passion — we’ll have talking points and signs ready to go!

description:

title: Sound the Alarm for Democracy

location.venue: Vigo County Annex Building of Terre Haute

description:
***If you are not from Terre Haute, Please start one of these near you! We would love this to be Nationwide!!!***

The Trump Administration and Elon Musk are acting with selfishness, hiding their actions in cowardice, and systematically dismantling the values upon which our country was built. The speed of the destruction has been truly horrific, and we the people are alarmed at the state of our democracy! So Indivisible Wabash Valley has launched the "Sound the Alarm for Democracy" weekly event. 

Every Monday at 12:05 pm, sound the panic on your car alarms, honk your horns, bang a drum, blow a trumpet, sing the Star Spangled Banner, or make noise however you can. The idea is that anyone can participate, no matter where they are, no matter what they are doing.

Those who are able will meet at the Vigo County Annex each week, everyone else, just make noise wherever you are: homes, schools, churches, jobs! We want to let our neighbors, our elected officials, and the rest of the world know that a lot of us are out here, still standing together to protect our democracy, and the rights to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness, fought for and defended for 250 years and counting.

JOIN US EVERY MONDAY!!
SOUND THE ALARM FOR DEMOCRACY

title: We The People Wednesdays in Walnut Creek
description:
This is a local Indivisible event organized by Indivisible ReSisters Contra Costa!  Join us every Wednesday evening from 5-6 p.m. at the corner of Ygnacio Valley Road and Civic Drive for a rousing honk and wave visibility action.  Bring your signs and raise your voice for democracy and to protect our rights!  

This is a nonviolent event. Stay within your rights, don’t break laws, stay safe, stay peaceful, and avoid any risk you don’t feel comfortable with. Don’t obstruct traffic, impede pedestrians, or commit any acts of property damage. If counterprotestors appear, do your best to ignore them.  When people shout from cars, just remember that we are standing for their rights, too.  They just don't know it.

This is a busy intersection and cars drive fast.  Please stay on the sidewalk at least a few feet from cars.  We can spread out down the block and take a stand on the pedestrian overpass.  Safety is our top priority.  If you have any concerns during this event, please find a peace ambassador in an orange vest and they will help.

There are several parking lots within walking distance or you can find street parking at Civic Park or on Civic Drive or Arroyo Way.

description:

We will not allow this administration’s attacks on the LGBTQ+ community to continue! #RESIST

We are being cosponsored by a local pride group, and have invited local pride groups to set up informational tables if they are available.

This is NOT business as usual in DC, this is NOT normal.

We need to stand up for due process, free speech, upholding court rulings, and the separation of church and state. The Founding Fathers established the principles of due process, free speech, and the separation of church and state through the First Amendment and other parts of the Constitution. These concepts were designed to protect individual rights and limit government power. 
We have NO KINGS in America, yet Trump is acting like one. 
We, the people, must rise up, and show that the power of the people is greater than the people in power.

title: Wheeler Salmonberry Trail Ground Building
description:
**Join The Salmonberry Trail in our exciting ground breaking event at Waterfront Park in Wheeler!**

The City of Wheeler is excited to announce that we are taking the first steps toward revitalization of Wheeler’s section of the Salmonberry Trail through partnership with the Salmonberry Trail Foundation and Tillamook Coast Visitors Association. We will be holding a **Ground Building event and ceremony on July 12, 2025 from 1:00-5:00 PM.** We truly could not be more excited for the recreational opportunities this trail will provide for our community.

This transformative project holds the potential to deliver lasting, meaningful benefits to our community. By linking the Willamette Valley to the Coast, it will not only strengthen regional connectivity but also invigorate rural tourism and empower small businesses. It champions public health and safe, active transportation options while expanding equitable access to the outdoors for all residents. Most importantly, it lays the foundation for sustainable infrastructure that will support our economy, environment, and quality of life for generations to come.

We will have local vendors, music, games, and a ribbon cutting ceremony celebrating the beginning of this coastal section of the trail. 
- July 12th, 1PM - 5PM
- Waterfront Park (500 Marine Dr, Wheeler, OR 97147)

---
**ABOUT THE SALMONBERRY TRAIL**
The Salmonberry Trail is an 82-mile multi-use path transforming a historic rail line into Oregon’s next big adventure. Connecting communities from the Willamette Valley to the coast, the trail will provide safe routes for recreation and education, expand economic opportunities, and improve public health. In partnership with local organizations, it will offer unique educational programs while promoting outdoor activity and conservation, making it a cornerstone of community development and environmental stewardship across the state.

**Wheeler Demonstration Project – Salmonberry Trail**
The Wheeler Demonstration Project is a short, high-impact segment of the Salmonberry Trail located in downtown Wheeler. This 1,800-foot trail segment runs north from Rector Street, across Hemlock Street, and along the bay side of the Oregon Coast Scenic Railway tracks adjacent to Botts Marsh. It features a compacted gravel path for pedestrians, designed to enhance safety and encourage walking in the downtown area.
Developed in partnership with the City of Wheeler, Oregon Coast Scenic Railway, Lower Nehalem Community Trust, and the Salmonberry Trail Foundation, the project supports local economic activity, offers environmental education through interpretive signage, and provides a model for similar efforts in other communities along the trail corridor.

description:
**Come to the Orange Plaza Square Park each week**, rain or shine, to take a stand opposing the oligarchs, billionaires and the regime that's attacking our way of life and the Constitution of the USA. Join our community in a nonviolent, peaceful demonstration! Make your voice heard. We are the many, they are the few that want to rule us all. Take a stand for democracy. Bring your signs, bring pots and pans, your whistles and kazoos and meet at the fountain - we'll spread out from there after a safety briefing. Let the people be heard! Let’s make some noise!

**GENERAL PROTEST/RALLY REMINDERS**

Remember the ABCs of protesting:

A) Always obey traffic signals and directions of the safety team!

B) Beware of detractors*! Do not talk to detractors or unaffiliated interviewers - doing so increases risks for all of us, including all the volunteers and organizers.

C) Chill vibes please! Never touch anyone else or their property (e.g., car, sign, backpack) without permission. Have fun! Build community!

*As our events become more popular, we may attract detractors and Trump/Elon/MAGA supporters, either passing in cars or as rally attendees. Some of their tactics are to act friendly, ask questions, and pretend to care about your answers. They may also gesture, yell, name-call, and use foul language. They often look to get a reaction they can capture on video. Do NOT engage with or speak to them. Do NOT answer their questions. Do NOT yell back at them or gesture (thumbs down, middle finger, etc.) Do NOT post photos or videos of them online. Do NOT reveal any personal or contact info to anyone at this or any rally you do not know to be on your side. If someone becomes threatening or violent, move away quickly and alert a safety volunteer, a police officer, and/or call 911. These guidelines keep you, our volunteers, and our organizers safe. Thank you!

**[Learn to de-escalate](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_Pgmn9QRr48&list=PLqIrQkVlKU3RZw0ytVd3U7XS3ofAaZItu&index=2)**

**[Learn to Grey-rock](https://health.clevelandclinic.org/grey-rock-method)**

Join us as we rise up to demand justice, accountability, and human rights! 

Avelo Airlines has accepted a $150 million contract with ICE to carry out deportation flights that violate constitutional rights. These flights tear families apart and deny people their legal right to due process — a right reaffirmed by the U.S. Supreme Court. This is a cruel, inhumane, and illegal partnership, and we’re coming together across the country to stop it.

On the last Sunday of Every Month, we’re joining forces with STOPAVELO.ORG National and Defend and Resist, to protest in cities across the U.S. This is a call to action for anyone who believes in democracy, human rights, and the rule of law.  

Together, we will:

Protest at Avelo-serviced airports nationwide

Boycott Avelo Airlines and push ticket sales to zero

Demand city and state officials cancel all Avelo contracts and subsidies

Shine a spotlight on this airline’s shameful role in aiding unlawful deportations

Join us at the airport protest. Your voice counts — and it’s needed now more than ever.

Let’s stand together against fascism, family separation, and corporate complicity.
No more silence. No more flights. #StopAvelo

#PeopleOverProfit #NoICEFlights #DueProcessForAll #IndivisibleCA27
#StopAvelo #DefendandResist

These protests will be in cooperation with larger national groups doing the same actions on those weekends. We want to make very clear to drivers what we are protesting about, so please make your signs, and other messaging specific to Avelo Airlines, civil rights, due process, etc.

address_lines: North Hamilton Street & East Trent Avenue

description:
We're doing something a little different this week standing up for Medicare and Medicaid.

We will stand at the corner of Trent and Hamilton.  Peaceful sidewalk protest. 

Medicaid is an essential program providing healthcare coverage for low-income individuals, families, and certain other populations, including children, pregnant women, and individuals with disabilities. It plays a crucial role in improving health outcomes, economic stability, and overall well-being for these populations. Medicaid also acts as a vital safety net for hospitals and providers, ensuring access to care for those who might otherwise be uninsured.

Medicare is crucial for providing financial security and health coverage to millions of older Americans and younger people with disabilities. It helps cover a wide range of medical expenses, including hospital stays, doctor visits, and prescription drugs. This coverage reduces the financial burden of healthcare, making it more accessible and affordable for beneficiaries.
While Trump, Elon, and their billionaire friends try to scam us into lining their pockets through completely unnecessary tax breaks for billionaires, they’re upending Medicaid and Medicare and attempting to rip away benefits from millions of Americans to make them happen.

For bridge protests, where visibility from a distance is crucial, the larger the lettering, the better. Here are some key considerations and general guidelines:
General Visibility Rules:
•	Distance is Key: The primary factor is how far away your audience will be. For highway overpasses, traffic might be moving quickly and at a significant distance.
•	"Rule of Thumb" for Legibility: A common guideline for outdoor signage is that each inch of letter height provides approximately 10 feet of legibility. So, for every 100 feet of viewing distance, you'd want at least 10-inch tall letters.
•	Bridge Specifics: Bridges often mean viewing from a greater distance than a sidewalk. Consider vehicles on the road below, and potentially other onlookers further away.
Practical Recommendations for Bridge Protests:
•	Go Big: Aim for lettering that is at least 12-24 inches tall, and even larger if possible. Some sources suggest using 20x30 or 24x30 inch boards for individual letters to create large, impactful messages.
•	Bold, Simple Fonts: Choose block, sans-serif fonts (like Arial or Helvetica) that are thick and easy to read. Avoid thin, ornate, or script fonts.
•	High Contrast Colors: This is critical!
o	Dark letters on a light background (e.g., black on white, dark blue on yellow) offer the best visibility.
o	Avoid low-contrast combinations like yellow on white or light blue on a pale background.
o	Limit your color palette to two or three colors for maximum impact and clarity.
•	Concise Messaging: Shorter messages with fewer words are easier to read quickly from a distance. Each letter takes up space, so a long message will require smaller letters to fit, reducing visibility.
•	Material and Construction:
o	Sturdy materials: Foam core boards or corrugated plastic are more rigid and durable than regular poster board, especially in windy conditions.
o	Weatherproof: Consider if rain or sun will affect your signs. Paint or vinyl letters are more resilient than marker.
o	Double-sided signs: If possible, make your signs double-sided to maximize visibility from different angles, especially for media coverage.
•	Test Your Signs: Before the protest, hold up your signs and have someone view them from a distance similar to what you expect on the bridge. This will help you determine if the lettering is large enough and if the message is clear.
•	Spacing (Kerning): Ensure there is adequate space between letters and words so they don't blend together from a distance.
By focusing on large, bold, high-contrast lettering and concise messages, you'll maximize the impact and readability of your bridge protest signs.

title: Weekly (Fri) Mass Pike Overpass Standout in Westfield - Southampton Rd (Routes 10/202)
description:
Wow! What a great location for a standout! On 5/30, around 17 people, including a bagpiper!  What a blast! LOTS of engagement with motorists!

There's lots and lots of traffic passing by. Southampton Road (Routes 10/202) is heavily traveled northbound and southbound, and the Mass Pike eastbound and westbound is below. Lots of honks and thumbs up and waves...and a few folks flying middle fingers. We smile and wave at them all! 

We'll have letterboards prepared for the lower part of the overpass fencing - the photo shows how that will look to folks passing on the Mass Pike. We're interacting with motorists on the Mass Pike, and on Southampton Road. We've discovered that the magic happens when we smile and wave to people!

Come when you can, and leave when you must. You needn't be present for the entire 1 1/2 hours.

### How to Get There

The address "130 Southampton Road, Westfield" will get you just north of the overpass. 

### Parking

We can't park in the Southampton Rd breakdown lane. There are vacant business properties north of the bridge, and it seems that parking would be OK there.

It looks like The Wealth Technology Group has vacated their office at 130 Southampton Rd, but the internet says that other businesses are located there, so please be mindful if you decide to park there.

### Etiquette!

We don't give the finger to people who give the finger to us, or who say unpleasant things. We smile and wave to them, too. 

We may see a counter protester. If so, the best thing to do is just ignore them and spend our time and energy waving to motorists. Let's keep things 100% non-confrontational in words and body language.

### Other Stuff

Please take everything you brought away with you, and leave the site totally clean.

If rain is predicted, we'll cancel. If we cancel, you'll receive an email notification.

### A Few Requests

We've found that roof rake sections make wonderful flagpoles and banner poles. If you have a roof rake (or 10’-15’ light metal poles or conduit) to contribute, we'll be happy to take it off your hands!

And, if you have an extra 3' x 5' American flag you're not using, we'd love it if you'd pass it on to us!

title: March to the Park!
description:
This a local Indivisible event!

Mark your calendars! Bring the kids! Join us on June 21st @ 10:30am for our March to the Park! from the Tuscarawas Co Courthouse to Tuscora Park (one mile). Join us afterwards for a potluck. Together with the League of Women Voters Tuscarawas County, we are collecting monetary donations for Jack’s House of Hope. 

Departure time: 10:45am! Bring your own signs to this event.

Signs

For this event, please bring your own signs. They can be on wood sticks such as tomatoe posts for ease of carrying. Make your message clear: Federal, state, and local issues of concern to you, your family, the community…there are just so many issues my head would explode if I wrote them all down. Pre-made signs will not be available for this event.

Monetary Donations

Together with the League of Women Voters of Tusc County, we are asking marchers to make a monetary donation of any amount for Jack’s House of Hope. Monetary donations for Jack’s House of Hope will be collected at Tuscora Park. Amanda Fontana, Friends of the Homeless of Tuscarawas County Board of Directors' Secretary will speak about the importance of our local shelter.

March, Eat, Chat, Play!

Our event is from 10:30am-12:30pm. We will march to Tuscora Park from the Tuscarawas County Courthouse and then share a covered dish and/or just bring something for yourself/your family, your own paper products/utensils, snacks to share, and good conversation with those joining us. If you bring something to share, please be mindful of allergies. An index card with a list of ingredients taped to the container would be appreciated. Label containers with your name if you want them back! Jenn Schrock will oversee the food/refreshments while we march.

Half of a covered pavilion near the bocce courts has been reserved for this event. Blankets and chairs can be dropped off beforehand. Marchers can carpool back to the Tusc Co Courthouse to then walk to the park (10:45am). For those that do not have a way back to the courthouse to march, Alicia Hall will help transport people to the courthouse BEFORE the march once they drop off their items at the park.

Remember: Bring your own signs to this event!

Kids can play on the playground equipment. Park rides and Putt-Putt golf open at NOON. See pricing at www.tuscorapark.com/park-info-contact.

We’ll take a group picture!

Helpers

We need helpers at the park to remain with the food, etc. until the marchers arrive. We also need help along the route, guiding marchers as they cross side streets. We don’t block traffic, we hold marchers on the sidewalk while traffic makes their turn left or right onto North Broadway. Let us know if you’re interested in helping.

Limited street parking is available around City Hall & across the South 1st ST Bridge at Auditorium Shores (use the Park ATX app with discount codes: FREE15ATX1, FREE15ATX2).

Nonviolent Protest Disclaimer: Nobody from our organization will be provocative and we are not planning civil disobedience. We are utilizing our First Amendment right to protest and our right to lobby our representative government. We do everything in our power to protect the civil rights and physical safety of everyone at our events. We have yet to have any significant incidents of safety issues at any of our events.

By attending our events, you are implicitly agreeing that while you attend our event, you will respect the laws and constitution of the United States and State of Texas and not create or contribute to a safety issue or lawlessness for our attendees and neighbors. title: Disappeared in America Visual Action
description:
**In America, the government doesn’t get to grab people off the streets, skip the courtroom, and send them straight to a foreign prison.** Disappeared in America is a national day of action to stand up for the rule of law and confront the Trump administration’s illegal abductions, detentions, and deportations of people like Kilmar Abrego Garcia, Rui Marras, and Juan Maldonado Zuniga. 

🚨**On Thursday, June 26th, we’re showing up at courthouses and town squares across the country to say: in America, we don’t let the government disappear people. That’s not who we are.**🚨

Americans believe in rule of law —and the courts are saying that due process is required. If a president can ignore the courts and disappear lawful residents, there is no limit to what can come next. President Trump has said he wants to abduct and deport U.S. citizens. If this isn’t stopped now, no one is safe.

**On June 26th we are launching a national photo petition day where people will take photos with posters of those who have been disappeared and flood social media with the truth.** 

A key focal point of this campaign will be to call on local sheriffs to refuse to cooperate with directives from ICE to engage in federal immigration enforcement, such as renting jail beds to ICE, participating in immigration raids, and transferring people to ICE detentions.  Sheriffs have wide discretion in how much they cooperate with ICE. Participation in federal immigration activities places additional burden on sheriffs’ offices and can erode local community trust in local law enforcement.

title: GOOD TROUBLE LIVES ON: Williamsburg, VA
description:
ALL OUR ACTIONS WILL BE PEACEFUL, RESPECTFUL and SAFE!!!

Our rights are under attack. Our democracy is under siege. We’ve been here before, and we know what to do.

On July 17, we honor the anniversary of the passing of civil rights hero John Lewis, not with ceremonies, but with action. Across the country, we will take to the streets, courthouses, and community spaces to carry forward his fight for justice, voting rights, and dignity for all.

This is more than a protest, it’s a moral reckoning. A continuation of the movement Lewis helped lead, and a new front in the struggle for freedom.

**Please note:** a core principle behind our John Lewis Good Trouble Day actions is a commitment to nonviolence in all we do. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

This is more than a protest, it’s a moral reckoning. A continuation of the movement Lewis helped lead, and a new front in the struggle for freedom.

COMMUNITY NORMS:

Please read before attending one of our events.

One of our main objectives is to host PEACEFUL, RESPECTFUL and SAFE EVENTS. Remember, when attending a Williamsburg JCC Indivisible event, your actions represent our group, and you are expected to conform to the Community Norms. Safety is a top priority for our attendees. We wish to remind everyone that we do not react to those drivers who make it clear they do not support us by aggravating them through screaming obscenities or making certain hand gestures. We do not want to enrage them and potentially make everyone, including other drivers, less safe. It is easier to wave at everyone and say, “Have a nice day”.

At our events, please do not hold signs or otherwise promote other events that Williamsburg JCC Indivisible is not hosting. You may be placing a potential legal liability onto our group that we are NOT willing to accept.

Please do not engage in DISRUPTIVE BEHAVIOURS! If you are asked to stop engaging in activities which are disrupting an event to the point people are complaining to the hosts that they are experiencing physical or emotional trauma, it is expected that you will be respectful of others and follow our Community Norms and stop those behaviours. Loud noises, such as, but not limited to, cowbells, horns, etc., are usually deployed by counter-protesters to disrupt an event, not by attendees participating in an event. If you refuse to disengage from such thoughtless behaviours, do not ruin the event for everyone else - please be kind and leave!

As with our previous events, the same rules apply. We will not engage with counter-protesters. If an issue arises, please notify one of the event organizers. At larger events, these organizers will be wearing Williamsburg JCC Indivisible T-shirts with yellow safety vests. We will not engage in any acts of violence or violation of any applicable laws or engage in civil disobedience. All actions will be peaceful. Everyone participating in this event will be required to behave lawfully to ensure the safety of event participants and will seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. We will obey the orders of authorized event marshals and law enforcement authorities. Event organizers will not be responsible for any injury or damage if any were to occur during this event. Each individual is responsible for the consequences of their actions and attends at their own risk. We will park in the Courthouse parking lot without blocking access lanes and will remove any trash that is left. We are committed to maintaining public health measures to practice safe protesting during these times. Please wear a mask and socially distance if that makes you more comfortable - weigh your own risk in attending. Follow all local safety guidelines at minimum, and any safety instructions from hosts that exceed local law.

location.venue: Sen. Angela Paxton Office and Watters Creek Village
address_lines: 10-11 AM: we will walk down the street to Paxton's Office at 604 S. Watters Road, Suite 100. Allen, TX 75013

description:
## Are you fed up with Texas legislators who don't represent Texans' best interests? So are we! Come stand up for your rights outside of State Senator Angela Paxton's office in Allen, TX. We will be on Bethany Dr at Watters Creek Village from 9-10 AM, and then walk to Paxton's office nearby at 604 S. Watters Road, Suite 100. Allen, TX 75013. We'll protest outside her office on Watters Rd. from 10-11 AM. Please bring food donations that will be given to Under My Umbrella, a local nonprofit that provides food for the needy, who will unfortunately be most harmed by MAGA's cruelty.

The TX lege just wrapped up one of its most harmful legislative sessions in state history, and the Republican majority in our legislature had a field day revoking Texans' rights. Here's a snapshot of what they "accomplished":

- school vouchers that take public tax dollars from public schools and give them to wealthy private school students and homeschoolers
- THC/marijuana ban
- extreme anti-abortion legislation
- book bans
- an attack on the separation of church and state; schools will now be required to post the Ten Commandments in classrooms

Almost no aspect of everyday life in Texas will be left untouched by the extremist, regressive legislation just passed by Texas Republicans.  Come stand in solidarity with your community as we protest outside of Texas State Senator Angela Paxton's office in Allen, TX. We demand representation and we will fight to repeal these harmful measures!

title: Avelo Airline Nationwide Protest
description:
**Indivisible Mesa is joining the Coalition to Stop Avelo's nationwide call to action for a full boycott of Avelo Airlines and organizing protests at all 54 airports where they operate.** Our goal? Drive ticket sales to ZERO and make Avelo feel the consequences of profiting from deportations.

On May 31st, Indivisible Mesa was part of the **26 protests across the country** who came together to protest Avelo Airlines on the same day for the first time! To keep the pressure on Avelo, the Coalition is planning to support additional nationwide protests and Indivisible Mesa is again joining the call!!

**Indivisible Mesa will be protesting against Avelo Airlines operating ICE deportations on Saturday, June 28th!** 

By protesting together, everywhere, on the same day, we elevate our anti-Avelo movement from a local news story to a can't miss national news story!

🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨🚨

The message to **Avelo** is simple: **"Cancel your contract with ICE."**

The message to **City Hall** is simple: **"Stop funding Avelo with local dollars."**

The message to **travelers** is simple: **"Boycott Avelo, don't give them your money."**

The message to **allies** is simple: **"Join us. Stand for justice. Fight inhumanity."**

And the message to the **world** is powerful: 
*We stand for families. 
We stand for immigration rights. 
We stand for due process. 
We stand for all Americans who are feeling scared and vulnerable. 
We stand against companies that sacrifice people for profit. 
We stand against blood money and we stand against deals-with-the-devil. We stand against Avelo's contract with ICE. 
And we stand together, together, together. 
We will win this fight! 
We will force Avelo to cancel its ICE contract.**

Protest locally, speak nationally.

✨Be safe, be lawful, be loud. Bring signs. Bring friends. Take pics.✨


==**Protest Information**==

🌄 Indivisible Mesa will be at the intersection of East Ray Rd and Power Rd.

🅿️ There is PLENTY of parking in the store surrounding the intersection, including Walmart, Target, etc. 

❄️Bring all the things to keep yourself cool like cooling towels, umbrellas for shade, water, etc. and feel free to bring extra for other protestors if you are able to!

🔥Indivisible Mesa leadership realizes it may be too hot for some to attend the event, but we have to be outside and as visible as possible. IT'S VITAL. **If this means you can only protest for 20 mins, then please come for 20 mins!! Everybody and every minute counts!!**


==**Signs & Graphics**==
Please create signs and graphics that are relevant to Avelo & Mesa Gateway Airport! The messaging we put on our signs can do a lot to cut right through Mesa Gateway's bureaucratic smokescreen. 

   ☑️ Call attention to Avelo Airlines separating families

   ☑️ Complicity of Mesa/Gateway airport

   ☑️ Illegal deportations without due process

   ☑️ Human trafficking

   ☑️ Rather overheat than let human trafficking continue

   ☑️ Print out large pics of ICE kidnapping people in Phoenix

Please share and bring friends to protest against these flights that are illegal, inhumane, & unconstitutional.

title: Disappeared in America Visual Action
description:
**In America, the government doesn’t get to grab people off the streets, skip the courtroom, and send them straight to a foreign prison.** Disappeared in America is a national day of action to stand up for the rule of law and confront the Trump administration’s illegal abductions, detentions, and deportations of people like Kilmar Abrego Garcia, Rui Marras, and Juan Maldonado Zuniga. 

🚨**On Thursday, June 26th, we’re showing up at courthouses and town squares across the country to say: in America, we don’t let the government disappear people. That’s not who we are.**🚨

Americans believe in rule of law —and the courts are saying that due process is required. If a president can ignore the courts and disappear lawful residents, there is no limit to what can come next. President Trump has said he wants to abduct and deport U.S. citizens. If this isn’t stopped now, no one is safe.

**On June 26th we are launching a national photo petition day where people will take photos with posters of those who have been disappeared and flood social media with the truth.** 

A key focal point of this campaign will be to call on local sheriffs to refuse to cooperate with directives from ICE to engage in federal immigration enforcement, such as renting jail beds to ICE, participating in immigration raids, and transferring people to ICE detentions.  Sheriffs have wide discretion in how much they cooperate with ICE. Participation in federal immigration activities places additional burden on sheriffs’ offices and can erode local community trust in local law enforcement.

_A core principle behind all Disappeared in America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values._

title: A Funeral for the Constitution - A Peaceful Protest of the Inaction of Senator Thom Tillis
description:
Join us on August 23, we will gather in downtown Greensboro dressed in black, not in celebration - but in mourning.
This solemn protest, led by concerned citizens across North Carolina, is a funeral march for our Constitution - the foundational document Senator Thom Tillis continues to undermine and nullify, piece by piece.
As we carry a symbolic coffin through the streets, accompanied by the haunting sound of a lone bagpipe, we will grieve the erosion of civil liberties, voting rights, and democratic norms. This is not a spectacle. This is a eulogy - for fairness, for accountability, and for a government of the people.

With peaceful resolve and powerful symbolism, we will honor what has been lost and demand better from those elected to serve us. We mourn, we march, and we resist - because democracy should not die in silence.

title: Get in Line, Senator Tillis
description:
This joyful protest gets in step for justice - literally.
"Joy is a form of resistance" is often attributed to the poet Toi Derricotte.

We're dancing to send a clear and unified message to Senator Thom Tillis: it's time to GET IN LINE with the people of North Carolina! While he continues to ignore the will of his constituents, we're responding not with silence, but with rhythm, joy and movement! Our feet will hit the ground in Guilford County on July 12, where every step is a stand - a stand for community building, for kindness, and for those whose voices have been sidelined.

With music, unity and purpose, we're turning this protest into a celebration and resistance into motion! Join us - because when we move together, we shift the future, and we won't stop dancing until our representatives fall in line with the people they serve!

title: NC: Pack the Court Against Racial Gerrymandering!

location.venue: Ward Federal Building, US District Courtroom #1

description:
We're taking the lawless NC legislature to court for rigging voting maps against the people of North Carolina — a scheme that unjustly comes at the expense of Black voters, especially. It's time to sound the alarm. Are you with us?

Our federal trial against gerrymandered maps continues on Friday, June 20, at the federal courthouse in Winston-Salem, and we're calling on YOU to join us in packing the court. We're expecting key testimony!

RSVP today to join us, We'll share more details about what to expect once you sign up!

*Please note: the schedules and timing of federal trials are subject to change. We'll keep you up-to-date every step of the way!

Federal Courthouse Etiquette:
Courtroom Etiquette:
• Be punctual! Arrive on time and account for the security check in at the entrance.
o All persons are required to show a valid U.S. government issued identification
card (federal or state). The identification must show, at minimum, a person’s
photo, name, and date of birth.
o REAL ID is NOT required. The REAL ID Act takes effect on May 7, 2025. However,
the Act does NOT apply to entry to federal courthouses, which is a
constitutionally protected activity. Although a picture identification must still be
shown to court security officers, it does not need to be a REAL ID-compliant
drivers license or identification card.
• No food, beverages, or chewing gum are permitted inside the courtrooms.
• Cell phones and electronic devices are PROHIBITED in the courthouse. You must leave
them in your car.
• While in the courtroom, and particularly when the court is in session, you must remain
silent.
• Courtroom-appropriate attire is expected when present in a courtroom. Hats and
sunglasses, unless for religious or medical reasons, should be removed before entering
the courtroom.
• Please stand when the judge enters and exits the courtroom.
• No smoking is allowed in the courthouse.
• Please do not speak to attorneys for the State Board of Election or to any of the
defendants.

title: FCTC Community Listening Session

location.venue: Orange Mound Library - Memphis Public Libraries

description: From Court to Classroom: Shifting the Truancy Narrative is a passion-led, two-phase campaign designed to build both understanding and support systems for students experiencing chronic absenteeism or truancy. We would like to invite you to phase 1 of the campaign. Phase 1 will focus on hosting a community listening session with 8–10 youth-centered organizations in Memphis to explore the social and structural barriers that contribute to school absenteeism. title: Elbows Up - Buffalo
description:
International Day of Action in Solidarity with Canada—Good Neighbors Getting It Done and Power to the People Western New York, will peacefully rally concerned members of the community to say, “We oppose President Trump's tariffs and threats to annex Canada as the 51st state. We will rally at Bufffalo’s Freedom Park on the American side of the Niagara River, and line up along the Bird Island Pier to wave to our Canadian friends in the Freedom Park in Fort Erie, Ontario.

title: Disappeared in America Visual Action
description:
**In America, the government doesn’t get to grab people off the streets, skip the courtroom, and send them straight to a foreign prison.** 

Disappeared in America is a national day of action to stand up for the rule of law and confront the Trump administration’s illegal abductions, detentions, and deportations of people like Kilmar Abrego Garcia, Rui Marras, and Juan Maldonado Zuniga. 

🚨**On Thursday, June 26th, we’re showing up at courthouses and town squares across the country to say: extrajudicial kidnappings have no place in our country. The USA is a nation founded on free speech, due process, and liberty. We will gather to demand the end of extrajudicial kidnappings by ICE and the Trump administration.**🚨

Americans believe in rule of law —and the courts are saying that due process is required. If a president can ignore the courts and disappear lawful residents, there is no limit to what can come next. President Trump has said he wants to abduct and deport U.S. citizens. If this isn’t stopped now, no one is safe.

**On June 26th we are launching a national photo petition day where people will take photos with posters of those who have been disappeared and flood social media with the truth.** 

A key focal point of this campaign will be to call on local sheriffs to refuse to cooperate with directives from ICE to engage in federal immigration enforcement, such as renting jail beds to ICE, participating in immigration raids, and transferring people to ICE detentions.  Sheriffs have wide discretion in how much they cooperate with ICE. Participation in federal immigration activities places additional burden on sheriffs’ offices and can erode local community trust in local law enforcement.

_A core principle behind all Disappeared in America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values._
accessibility_notes:

title: #TeslaTakedown Santa Monica
description:
Elon Musk is destroying our democracy, and he's using the fortune he built at Tesla to do it. We are taking action at Tesla to stop Musk's illegal coup.

⚡Sell your Teslas, dump your stock, join the picket lines.

⚡ We're tanking Tesla's stock price to stop Musk.

⚡Stopping Musk will help save lives and protect our democracy.

The stakes couldn’t be higher. No one is coming to save us. Not politicians, not the media, not the courts.

Tesla Showroom: 300 Broadway (intersection of Third & Broadway)

Tesla Takedown is a peaceful protest movement. We oppose violence, vandalism and destruction of property. This protest is a lawful exercise of our First Amendment right to peaceful assembly.

PRO TIPS:

☮️ Please do not engage hecklers or single out individual drivers in a threatening way. Winning hearts and minds is the only way we will accomplish our goals. Aggression will be eagerly documented by our foes and used to discredit our message.

☮️ We support everyone’s right to free speech. However, the national #TeslaTakedown movement recently issued guidance to please reduce usage of “swastika” symbols on signs. Elon Musk has, of course, earned his popular association with such ugly symbols, but we risk being misconstrued or offending potential allies by having them all over our signs. Again, winning as many hearts and minds as possible is our aim.

☮️ Bring shade and water if it’s a sunny day. It can get pretty hot out there, especially if you’re dancing and singing with us :)

#TeslaTakedown #BoycottTesla #BoycottMusk

description: The Santa Fe chapter of Veterans For Peace started this vigil in 2002 and have continued it every Friday at noon for 23 years. Its purpose is to bring awareness to the hundreds of billions of our tax dollars going to the production of new nuclear weapons here in our state. Many people, even many New Mexicans, are unaware that Los Alamos National Lab is currently building several new bomb factories to increase production of nuclear bomb cores (known as plutonium "pits") to reach a goal of 30 to 120 new pits per year. Each pit, on average, has the destructive power of 20 Hiroshima-sized bombs. Loud public outcry may be able to halt this waste of federal money, or at least slow it down until we elect a saner administration. Life on Earth is at stake.

title: Save Our Libraries
description:
This a local Indivisible event!

Indivisible McHenry County is hosting a protest rally to show our opposition to the Trump administration's proposed elimination of the IMLS (Institute of Museum and Library Services), which will affect us on a local level. The rally will take place on Friday, June 20th, in front of the McHenry Public Library, 809 Front St (Rte 31), McHenry, from 3 p.m. until 5 p.m.

On June 6th, a Federal judge gave the Trump administration permission to proceed with dismantling the IMLS even though there is another lawsuit underway that is trying to save the agency through a different Federal court.

The IMLS was created and funded by Congress in 1996 for the purpose of providing support to libraries and museums in every state in the U.S. The agency has had bipartisan support throughout its history, with reauthorization occurring under the Clinton, George W. Bush, Obama, and Trump administrations. The IMLS is required by law to conduct activities that support libraries and to provide reports to Congress on important issues. The devastating cuts to the IMLS’s grants and services will make it impossible for the agency to operate as required by Congress. 

Although libraries in McHenry County do not rely on the IMLS for most of their funding, the elimination of the IMLS could still result in cuts to library services that are enjoyed by our residents and tens of thousands of other people in Illinois. The IMLS provides millions of dollars in funding to the Illinois State Library that is used to fund RAILS (Reaching Across Illinois Libraries System), the government agency that assists more than 4000 library facilities in Illinois, including all of the libraries in McHenry County.

RAILS provides the interlibrary delivery service which allows library patrons to check out books and other items from any library within the Illinois system. RAILS also provides: a shared electronic catalog and cataloging support • group purchases and member discounts that helps libraries to save money • continuing education and consulting resources to library employees and trustees • content services for online publishing • grant opportunities for local libraries • and many other valuable services. If the IMLS is eliminated it is unlikely that RAILS will be able to survive, and all of the valuable services that it provides to our residents will also be eliminated. Let your voice be heard. Please join us on June 20th.

Indivisible Baltimore County supports and exercises the constitutional right to peaceful assembly and free expression. We do not condone violence, property damage, or actions that interfere with public safety. Each individual is responsible for their own conduct.

The Trump Administration is cutting back many of this country's vital services, while at the same time ramping up ICE enforcement. They aim to spend $48 billion dollars to expand immigration detention, while firing federal workers, cutting vital community services and eliminating the Department of Education. We don’t want to live in their police state. We don't want a system that terrorizes and kidnaps our immigrant brothers and sisters, while it cuts and eliminates our vital education, nutrition and healthcare services!

We reject the Trump administration’s cruel treatment of immigrant people. We reject the terror ICE inflicts on our immigrant communities. We reject the violation of the rights of ALL people to due process. We stand in solidarity with all working people and students. And so we are gathering every Monday to say to this Administration:

Stop hurting human beings! Stop hurting immigrant people! Stop violating human rights! Stop dividing us and stripping our communities of the resources we need to live dignified and fulfilling lives! Stop building up a surveillance and police state while eliminating the vital services we require to live!

Why we are standing up and fighting back:

To support our immigrant communities that are under attack. Kilmar Abrego Garcia, Elsy Berrios, Mahmoud Khalid, Rumeysa Ozturk, and countless others have had their right to due process violated by ICE and DHS. We fight for the justice they deserve.

To demand accountability for the police and surveillance state that is enveloping our communities, and threatening the privacy rights of human beings to exist free of intrusion and overreach from the State.

To demand accountability for the extrajudicial operations of ICE and DHS.

We are standing up, refusing to obey in advance, and saying no to fascism!

Join us every Monday for a peaceful #EyesOnICE protest as Baltimore takes a stand against this Administration and its cruel anti-human, anti-immigrant, anti-worker, anti-student agenda.

#EyesOnICE

#BringKilmarHome

#FreeElsyBerrios

#FreeThemAll

#AbolishICE

title: Weekly (Tues) I-91 Overpass Standout - Mtn Park Rd, Holyoke, MA
description:
Bring a friend!!!

Come out to show that ordinary people can raise their voices against the chaos and destruction of this Administration. Help remind folks that they, too, can stand up for their beliefs - and that there's lots and lots of people who aren't on board with the "cruelty as entertainment" behavior of Trump and Musk and the GOP.

### Recent DOT Visits

A Department of Transportation employee visited twice in the three weeks prior to 5/20 to ask that people NOT attach anything to the fencing. On 5/20, he parked and waited until everything was removed from the fencing. It seems reasonable to expect that DOT enforcement will continue. We haven't seen him lately, but...

### How to Get There

The address "9 Mountain Park Rd, Holyoke" will get you there if you're using Waze. (Mountain Park Road runs off Route 5, and is not accessible from I-91.) People have reported that some GPS systems bring you right under the bridge, but on I-91. That’s annoying!

Please park on the side of the road before the bridge. We can't park on the bridge.

### Other Stuff

Please take everything you brought away with you, and leave the site totally clean.

If rain is predicted, we'll cancel. If we cancel, you'll receive an email notification.

We may see a counter protester. If so, the best thing to do is just ignore them and spend our time and energy waving to motorists. Let's keep things 100% non-confrontational in words and body language.

### A Few Requests

We've found that roof rake sections make wonderful flagpoles and banner poles. If you have a roof rake (or 10’-15’ light metal poles or conduit) to contribute, we'll be happy to take it off your hands!

Donations...we've purchased banners and grommets and flags and zip ties and bungee cords, and we'll be getting more. We’ve purchased 20” x 30” letter boards for messaging we can change. All this costs $$$. We'll have a bucket for donations, and if you could throw something in, that'd be great. And if not, that's perfectly OK, too - your presence is what's really important. See where the money's going! https://tinyurl.com/IN-SLWMProtestTeamFinancials

title: Celebrate Your Independence: Rally & March
description:
Celebrate Your Independence: Rally & March

Worcester City Hall (Front) | 12–2 PM | Friday, July 4, 2025

Worcester Indivisible invites you to celebrate independence YOUR way with us on the 4th of July from 12:00PM-2:00PM, at Worcester City Hall on the very spot the Declaration of Independence was first read in New England. 

DECLARE YOUR TRUTHS TO BE SELF EVIDENT. 

Whether your version of freedom and independence revolves around women’s reproductive rights, LGBTQ+ equality, ICE and immigration, Indigenous and First People rights to tribal land and sovereignty, food insecurity, housing affordability, or racial justice and equality for all, these are the fundamental principles the Declaration of Independence and the 4th of July are built on. Ignored, dismissed and unlawfully obstructed by the current Trump administration, it is to you, the people of these United States, that we must look to in order to make us whole and declare our sovereignty as a united people. 

WE THE PEOPLE DECLARE OUR INDEPENDENCE. 

Please join us for a day of declaration, celebrating our freedom of diversity and independence from a tyrannical administration by asserting the fundamental rights granted to us by both the Declaration of Independence and the United States Constitution. Let us declare our truths and rights to be self evident by making our voices heard and coming together as the diverse and united community we are, can and should be. Come with your families, wear your best 4th finery or regalia celebrating your individual expressions of independence, to enjoy good food from local food trucks, inspirational speakers, music, and tables with resources!

We must seize this opportunity to make our voices heard on the future of our cherished public lands! 



Rally Details:

Date: Monday, June 23, beginning at 3:30 pm
Meeting Point: De Vargas Park (a few blocks from the El Dorado Hotel)
What: Peaceful rally and march to the El Dorado Hotel (WGA meeting location)
Message: New Mexicans love our public lands, and we want to keep public lands in public hands! 


We need you there: Plan to bring friends, family, and anyone who cares about our public lands. Come with signs supporting public lands and national monuments. We need to organize a HUGE turnout for this peaceful rally and march. Please share far and wide!



As New Mexicans, we love our public lands and believe they belong in public hands. Our shared love for these special places unites us. Let's come together to make sure these leaders hear that message loud and clear!
More details to follow soon!

title: Leaving MAGA: Budget Cuts will not Heal
description:
The Big Ugly Bill will add 3.8 trillion to the national debt while stripping many Americans of their earned benefits like Medicaid. Cuts to benefits never heal! This bill also strips states of their rights to regulate AI which will have long lasting implications from work to access to clean water for all of us. These cuts to our benefits are traded for tax breaks for billionaires and unregulated AI will only further benefit the already obscenely wealthy. Americans are frustrated on all sides and we welcome folks to leave MAGA and join us in standing up for our earned benefits and the rights of our states to regulate AI. 

If you or someone you know is thinking of leaving the MAGA train there is support available. leavingMAGA.com provides a nonjudgmental community for those looking for folks with similar stories and concerns.

United we stand.

title: Small Town, Loud Voices - El Segundo
description:
This a local Indivisible event organized by El Segundo residents to stand in solidarity with our communities and stand up to the Trump administration.

This will be a family-friendly, dog-friendly, non-violent, no-vandalism, community event. We'll be staying on the grassy areas and out of the roads. Please keep it friendly, and if there is any negativity or counter-protestors, don't engage. We'll have folks on hand who can help de-escalate any situation if necessary.

What this event is:

* This is a stationary, “honk and wave” visibility event at a location that sees a lot of weekend traffic.

* This is a positive, peaceful, community-focused, and family- and dog-friendly event.

What this event is not:

* This is not a march, and there is no programming/planned speaker.

* This is not a civil disobedience event. We will not block roads, sidewalks, or the entrances of any buildings.

* We will not be engaging with any hecklers. The El Segundo Police Department is aware of the event and available to help assist to keep everyone safe if there are counter-protestors.

There are many other Indivisible events across LA, so if this doesn't sound like what you're looking for, please feel free to attend a different event.

Details:

* 10 AM to 12 PM

* Grassy area in front of the El Segundo sign at the corner of Main & Imperial in El Segundo. We will expand to the grassy area across Main if necessary.

* There is street parking along Imperial Avenue (not Imperial Highway) within El Segundo, as well as on the surrounding streets south of Imperial Ave.

* Please do not park illegally (i.e. blocking driveways or in the local businesses’ lots). We want to bring people in to our movement, not turn them off!

We can't wait to see you. We are looking forward to making our voices heard together!

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

title: Quacco Road Protest
description:
In solidarity with local organizer Alex Morales Borralles, who bravely started this protest on his own on Quacco Road and the Coastal Highway a few weeks ago, Coastal Georgia for Democracy calls for Savannah to support the Spanish-language-speaking residents of Chatham County who are in danger in the more rural areas of the county near Savannah.

Alex starts his protest around 5 p.m. on Fridays, though some of his support is not able to show up until 6 p.m. Please join him any time between 5:30-7 p.m. on the sidewalks of the intersection of Quacco Road and Route 17 (Coastal Highway) with signs that support our immigrant community in the face of ICE raids in conjunction with the Chatham County Sheriff's Office (CCPD).

title: Hey Senators, What are you Doing? Rally-Brenham TX Saturday June 21st
description:
Join us this Saturday for a "Hey Senators, what are you doing?" rally. June 21st 11a-2p, this is a Rain or Shine rally. 

Many will focus this week  on the current Big bill now in the Senate. This bill includes the extension of tax cuts for the very wealthy, cuts to Medicaid, SNAP, Medicare, Vet Services  & more all of which will all be detrimental to rural areas, hospitals & nursing homes. Any changes the Senate makes will push the bill back to the house giving us more opportunities to protest changes.

These events have been wonderful and are giving people opportunities to express their dissent, meet new friends, exchange ideas and have an amazing sense of camaraderie! 

We will meet behind Taco Bell in the Walmart parking lot close to the trees. Please park in this area & walk down to our easement location in front of Taco Bell. Taco Bell has been very accommodating to our efforts. They request that no vehicles park in front of their trash area even though it is marked for parking. Please consider patronizing Taco Bell at these events. Please do not block business customer parking. Lastly, please do not leave any trash.

title: LGBTQ+/ DEI & Stonewall Riots 56 Years Later Rally-Brenham Saturday, June 28th
description:
The Stonewall riots, which began on June 28, 1969, are widely considered the catalyst for the modern LGBTQ+ rights movement and the inspiration for Pride celebrations. A police raid on the Stonewall Inn, a gay bar in New York City, sparked days of protests and clashes, bringing attention to the systemic discrimination and violence faced by the LGBTQ+ community. 
We will also celebrate the Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion in our Country. Three interconnected concepts that create fair and welcoming environments for people of all backgrounds. We MUST STAND UP & PROTECT these issues. 

These events have been wonderful and are giving people opportunities to express their dissent, meet new friends, exchange ideas and have an amazing sense of camaraderie! 

We will meet behind Taco Bell in the Walmart parking lot close to the trees. Please park in this area & walk down to our easement location in front of Taco Bell. Taco Bell has been very accommodating to our efforts. They request that no vehicles park in front of their trash area even though it is marked for parking. Please consider patronizing Taco Bell at these events. Please do not block business customer parking. Lastly, please do not leave any trash.

title: Disappeared in America: Stand up against Fascism
description:
In America, the government doesn’t get to grab people off the streets, skip the courtroom, and send them straight to a foreign prison. Disappeared in America is a national day of action to stand up for the rule of law and confront the Trump administration’s illegal abductions, detentions, and deportations of people like Kilmar Abrego Garcia, Rui Marras, and Juan Maldonado Zuniga.

On Thursday, June 26th, we’re showing up at courthouses and town squares across the country to say: **that’s not who we are.**

** Please bring posters of the disappeared: [click here to print](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-L_9i7If6RS-mNLgxWqm_DcZWT9o5xnu). **

It’s essential that we show people in our own communities and across the country that Americans reject the violation of due process, stand with those targeted by the Trump administration, and are willing to take action to raise awareness and prevent local authorities from participating in these illegal and unjust practices.

This issue is not a partisan one, it’s a matter of rule of law and a moral question. Do we want to live in a country where anyone can be taken without warning and without rights? What happens next if we don’t act now?

**It's Blue Turn Indivisible as part of the Not Above the Law coalition**

Good Trouble Lives On is a national day of action to respond to the attacks on our civil and human rights by the Trump administration. Together, we’ll remind them that in America, the power lies with the people.

Good Trouble Lives On is a national day of nonviolent action to respond to the attacks posed on our civil and human rights by the Trump administration and to remind them that in America, the power lies with the people. 

On July 17, the anniversary of Congressman John Lewis’s passing, we’re taking action across the country to defend our democracy and carry forward his legacy of Good Trouble.

From voter suppression bills like the SAVE Act to the criminalization of protest, the Trump administration is launching a full-scale attack on our civil and human rights. But we know the truth: in America, the power lies with the people, and we’re rising to prove it.

This is more than a protest; it’s a moral reckoning. A continuation of the movement Lewis helped lead, and a new front in the struggle for freedom.

**Please note:** A core principle behind our Good Trouble Lives On actions is a commitment to nonviolence in all we do. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

description:

Wear your NO KINGS shirts if you have them.

We continue to show up and bear witness to our federal elected officials. Meet on the sidewalks near the roundabout at Pinnacle Hills and West Northgate. (Stay out of the middle of the roundabout.) *Rain or shine, but be weather aware.*

description:

For further information, check out CNN's recent story exposing the lie that Iran is close to developing nuclear weapons:

https://www.cnn.com/2025/06/17/politics/israel-iran-nuclear-bomb-us-intelligence-years-away

title: Don't Stop Me Now: A No Kings Protest in North Phoenix
description:
Last Saturday, we made history with the largest U.S. protest ever.

Thousands of us stood up with one voice:

**No Kings. No Cronies.**  
We’re holding Donald Trump and CD-8 Representative Abe Hamadeh accountable to the people they’re supposed to represent.

We’re not stopping now.

Join us in North Phoenix for another high-visibility sidewalk protest to keep the momentum going — peaceful, powerful, and impossible to ignore.

If you stood with us last week, bring a friend and show up again. If you missed it, now’s your chance.

We’re moving fast. We’re staying loud. We’re not backing down.

**Important Reminders:**  
- Keep signs peaceful, family-friendly, and on message  
- Be respectful to the community and local businesses  
- Stay on public sidewalks — do not block traffic or driveways  
- Bring water, wear sun protection, and prepare for heat

**No Kings. No silence. Let’s go.**

title: Proud and Free: United for Trans Power

location.venue: Cathedral of Hope United Church of Christ, Interfaith Peace Chapel

description:
Join us for #ProudandFree: United for Trans Power¨ 

The Supreme Court is expected to issue a decision soon in U.S. v. Skrmetti, a case led by Lambda Legal and ACLU that could impact trans rights and access to healthcare across the country.

No matter the outcome, we are coming together in a "PROUD AND FREE: National Week of Action" to support trans people, push back on disinformation, and affirm that our communities are united for trans power.

🏛️ What is U.S. v. Skrmetti? A lawsuit filed by @ACLU, @LambdaLegal, @ACLU of Tennessee and Akin Gump on behalf of transgender youth and their families challenging Tennessee’s categorical ban (SB1) on gender-affirming medical care for transgender youth.

🏳️‍⚧️ Why does it matter? This case is about the constitutionality of states banning access to critical medical care for trans minors, particularly gender-affirming care. This could have nationwide impact on access to care, trans rights, and other sex-based discrimination by the government. 

JOIN US in an action in your community for activations various days after the decision in support to the trans community!

title: Protect Trans Youth: Chicago Demands Healthcare Access Now!
description:
On Saturday (6/21) at Noon, the streets of Chicago will rise in solidarity with trans and gender nonconforming youth across the nation, and especially those in Tennessee. The Supreme Court's recent 6-3 decision, allowing Tennessee's discriminatory ban on access to gender-affirming care for youth, is a devastating blow to human rights and the well-being of a vulnerable population.

This is not just a protest; it's a powerful declaration that access to life-saving healthcare is a fundamental right, not a privilege to be denied. We will stand united to show the country that trans youth deserve to thrive, to receive the care they need, and to live free from discrimination.

Why Your Presence Matters:

Show Solidarity: Stand with trans youth, their families, and allies who are fighting for their right to essential healthcare.

Demand Justice: Send a clear message to the Supreme Court and legislative bodies that discriminatory bans on healthcare will not be tolerated.

Amplify Voices: Help raise awareness about the critical importance of gender-affirming care and its positive impact on mental and physical health.

Build Community: Connect with fellow advocates and strengthen our collective power to fight for LGBTQ+ equality.

Let's make our voices heard loud and clear from Chicago: Healthcare is a human right. No bans, no surrender!

What: Protest and Rally in Solidarity with Trans Youth
When: Saturday at Noon
Where: Federal Plaza
Bring: Signs, water, comfortable shoes, and your unwavering commitment to justice!

Together, we can push back against these harmful decisions and ensure a future where all youth, including trans and gender nonconforming youth, have the support and care they deserve. See you there!

🏛️ What is U.S. v. Skrmetti? A lawsuit filed by @ACLU, @LambdaLegal, @ACLU of Tennessee and Akin Gump on behalf of transgender youth and their families challenging Tennessee’s categorical ban (SB1) on gender-affirming medical care for transgender youth.

🏳️‍⚧️ Why does it matter? This case is about the constitutionality of states banning access to critical medical care for trans minors, particularly gender-affirming care. This could have nationwide impact on access to care, trans rights, and other sex-based discrimination by the government.

description:

title: Proud and Free: United for Trans Power in Santa Barbara, California
description:
Join us for #ProudandFree: United for Trans Power this Saturday

WHEN: Saturday, June 21st, 11:00 - 11:30 am. 

WHERE: Santa Barbara County Courthouse, 1100 Anacapa St, Santa Barbara, CA 93101

On Wednesday, the U.S. Supreme Court issued a devastating decision in U.S. v. Skrmetti, ruling to block access to potentially life-saving medical care that allows trans people to live their lives as they see fit.

U.S. v. Skrmetti is a lawsuit filed by the ACLU, Lambda Legal, the ACLU of Tennessee, and Akin Gump on behalf of transgender youth and their families challenging Tennessee’s categorical ban (SB1) on gender-affirming medical care for transgender youth.

The Court’s ruling against trans youth, their families, and their doctors threatens the well-being of trans people, the safety of our communities, and the ability of every family to determine what is best for them. It is an attack on the right of each of us to control our own future.

In Santa Barbara and across the United States, we will gather in community to say that we believe our freedom to be ourselves is worth fighting for. No matter what the challenges, we will always be proud and free.

Join us this Saturday, June 21 from 11:00-11:30 am in front of the Santa Barbara County Courthouse as we unite in solidarity for trans freedom, joy, and power with activists across the country organized by the ACLU and Lambda Legal. Help us to take on bullies, build trans power, and do our part so that trans youth grow up to be happy, healthy trans adults. Learn more about the harmful decision, the implications for gender-affirming care, threats to gender-affirming care in California, and the next steps to stay involved in our fight for a better future for trans people across the country.

No matter what the Court or politicians say, transgender youth and their families are not alone. We will continue to fight in courtrooms and communities across the country to ensure all people have the freedom to shape their own futures.

WHAT: Proud and Free: United for Trans Power 
WHEN: Saturday, June 21st, 11:00 - 11:30 am. 
WHERE: Santa Barbara County Courthouse
1100 Anacapa St, Santa Barbara, CA 93101

This event is hosted by the Santa Barbara Transgender Advocacy Network in partnership with Pacific Pride Foundation, PFLAG Santa Barbara, and Planned Parenthood California Central Coast.

title: Bigger Than Dobbs II: Stop Trump's War on Women
description:
Bigger Than Dobbs II: Stop Trump's and the GOP's War on Women

March Forward/Indivisible Quincy is organizing a "Bigger Than Dobbs'' rally to Stop the War on Women, Sunday 6/29 from 2-4 pm in the Hancock Adams Common outside Quincy City Hall. Speakers will include local activists, organizations, and elected officials. Some signs will be provided, but feel free to bring your own!

Our event is part of a weekend of action supported by Indivisible and the Women's March to mark the anniversary of the Supreme Court's Dobbs decision, sadly overturning the decades of case law for Roe vs Wade. In the barrage of attacks on our democracy, it is marginalized groups and women who are the targets. Despite our warnings and protests, the current Republican party, with Donald Trump at the helm, have accelerated their plan to implement Project 2025.

Their plan to restore a white, Christian patriarchy was clearly stated in Project 2025. We warned that Republicans were "turning back the clock" and that "abortion was just the tip of the iceberg."  Each section detailed how the freedoms of women would be curtailed. As we pointed out, abortion bans are just the beginning. Their aim is to put women back into traditional "Biblically-based marriages," without careers or reproductive rights or even the right to vote, and to punish those who won't abide by their rules. 

In the time since SCOTUS ruled to overturn Roe, we have seen a degradation of democracy across the board while attacks on women have been quietly happening. There aren't armed, masked men abducting women who won't comply (yet) but it’s clear - from the cancellation of medical research pertaining to women, to the firings of top female military officials, to voter suppression law specifically targeting married women, the GOP War on Women must be stopped. This is our message: Stop Trump's War on Women!

*A core principle behind all Indivisible events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

title: Proud and Free: United for Trans Power
description:
Join us for #ProudandFree: United for Trans Power¨ 

The Supreme Court is expected to issue a decision soon in U.S. v. Skrmetti, a case led by Lambda Legal and ACLU that could impact trans rights and access to healthcare across the country.

No matter the outcome, we are coming together in a "PROUD AND FREE: National Week of Action" to support trans people, push back on disinformation, and affirm that our communities are united for trans power.

🏛️ What is U.S. v. Skrmetti? A lawsuit filed by @ACLU, @LambdaLegal, @ACLU of Tennessee and Akin Gump on behalf of transgender youth and their families challenging Tennessee’s categorical ban (SB1) on gender-affirming medical care for transgender youth.

🏳️‍⚧️ Why does it matter? This case is about the constitutionality of states banning access to critical medical care for trans minors, particularly gender-affirming care. This could have nationwide impact on access to care, trans rights, and other sex-based discrimination by the government. 

JOIN US in an action in your community for activations various days after the decision in support to the trans community!

📍 Event details coming soon! Please find events in your state or city.

title: Bethel Defends Democracy: Whose Country? OUR Country!
description:
Please join us for our 16th consecutive rally to Defend Democracy in beautiful downtown Bethel. While our overall theme is Defending Democracy, each week we pick a specific focus. On Saturday June 21st, 11am - noon,  back at PT Barnum Square, our focus is to bask in the success of our No Kings rally:
Whose Country? OUR Country!

We are said NO to authoritarianism. 
We are said NO to fascism. 
We are said NO to a dictatorship. 

We are sharing the square this week with our town's Music in the Park event which will start on our square at 12:30pm.  Their event is weather permitting but we are rain or shine or unbearable humidity (good thing we have some lovely large trees for shade).  So come rally for a while, enjoy lunch in town and then some music in the park!

We'll rally with our signs and take a short march. We also like to end each week with a sing-a-long.

The rally is non-partisan. What this means is that like-minded people from diverse backgrounds are participating and are vital to our rallies. Defending Democracy crosses party lines: we have registered Republicans, Unaffiliated, Democrats, and non-voters, all coming together to fight for the rights of “We the People” to determine the type of society we want to live in.

A sign-making table will also be available, complete with all the necessary supplies, for young and old to make signs for the rally.

We also collect a non-perishable food item for our local food pantry each week. The food pantry greatly appreciates the donations each week!  Anything you want to contribute is welcome, but some special requests from the food pantry include:

sunscreen

bug spray

Neither can be bought with SNAP but are vital for folks working outdoors in the summer or for kids who will be attending outdoor camps while school is out. Smaller containers that would fit inside a lunchbox are ideal size!

 We are currently lowest on baking supplies, pudding, and jello. Pudding and jello can either be the box mix or predone cups. 

Spices, Coffee and Baking supplies are always needed.

Individually packaged items. If you bought a variety pack of something like granola bars or instant oatmeal and discovered there's a flavor you won't eat, please give us the individual packs out of box.

Empty egg cartons- Any style, so long as they're clean.

SMALL empty detergent bottles

Note: Rally is rain or shine.

We ask that attendees refrain from sign holding or chanting at the curb during our speaking portion of the rally. We have had issues with speakers being heard because of the increased honking. It also is a courtesy to the speakers who are often discussing serious and sensitive topics. We are sharing a small square so we need your help to make the rallies comfortable for everyone.

We have tried to arrange the rallies so there is a little something for everyone: chanting, marching, themes with speakers, live music, fun trinkets, sign making. We appreciate every one of you that attends and we are working hard to bring all of us together to voice our frustrations, build community and also hopefully learn a little something from experts or your fellow neighbors experiences.

We appreciate your understanding and cooperation. ❤️

We also ask that you park at one of the four public parking lots. The lots that are the closest to the rally location, the Municipal Center, are the lot behind the municipal center and the train station lot on Durant Ave.

Although all street parking is public, we ask that you please not park in the limited parking spots in front of our local businesses, but definitely enjoy our beautiful towns restaurants and shops after the rally! 
Thank you 😊
